back: HRM that achieves financial, social and ecological goals, inside and outside the organization, long term, controlling for side effects and negative feedback.
Social (people & community) · ecological (environmental impact) · financial (profitability & investments).

front: Strategic vs sustainable HRM – scope & time
back: Own organization → also communities and other organizations; shorter → longer-term orientation.

front: Strategic vs sustainable HRM – control & role
back: Top-down → top-down + bottom-up; reactive → proactive & activist; implementer → initiates and sustains change.
Financial performance most important → environmental, social, financial of equal importance.

front: Reasons for sustainable HRM (Stahl et al., 2020)
back: Compliance (sanctions, obligations) · instrumental (strategy, talent, investors) · mission-led (do the right thing). Last two go beyond the law.
Hire for sustainability values, link green behaviour to promotion, eco-education.
Volunteering, positive work environment, health investments, no child/forced labour in supply chain, decent pay.
HR contributes: excessive pressure, biased algorithms, precarious contracts, extreme pay gaps, layoffs for short-term profit.
HR fails to prevent: harassment, pay inequality, unsafe conditions, discrimination in promotion, not developing workers threatened by AI.
